topic: Bhava bala — how house strength is actually computed (DD deep-dive reel, English, 2026-09-04 pm)

slides.sub: Everyone says a house is "strong". The texts actually compute it.

slides.body:
Bala means strength. Bhava bala is the classical scheme for scoring a house — not a planet — as a quantity you can actually compare against another house.

It sits beside Shadbala, the six-fold strength system for planets. Same instinct, different subject: Shadbala scores the actors, Bhava bala scores the stages they act on.

The strength of the house lord, carried over from that planet's own Shadbala score.

This is the largest single input, and it is the one intuition already reaches for — a house whose lord is strong is a house that can deliver. The scheme simply makes it numeric instead of impressionistic.

Each house gains strength from a direction, in the same way planets do in their own digbala.

The classical assignment ties houses to the cardinal directions, and a house is credited according to how well its position agrees with the direction it favours. It is a small contributor, but it is part of the stated computation and gets dropped constantly.

The net effect of aspects falling on the house. Benefic aspects add, malefic aspects subtract, and the result can be negative.

This is why a house with a strong lord can still underperform: a well-scored lord and a heavily afflicted house are two different measurements, and Bhava bala keeps them separate on purpose.

points: Comparison — which of two houses is better placed to deliver
Ranking — the classical texts rank all twelve and read the extremes
Pair it with Ashtakavarga, the benefic-point system, as a second opinion
Dasha still supplies the timing — bala says capacity, never when

slides.body:
Bhava bala is computed differently across texts and software, so two programs can hand you two scores for the same chart. Treat it as a relative measure inside one chart, never as an absolute grade, and never compare a score across two people's charts.

And a low score is not a sentence. It describes capacity under conditions, which dasha and effort both move.

Pull the Bhava bala table your software already computes and look only at the top two and bottom two.

Comment which house came out strongest, and save this reel — the three components are the whole scheme.
